entry.hook: The Adamantine Band is not a weapon. It is a jaw—a ring forged to bite down on any power that dares to rise against its master. A single throw of this band can disarm a god, collapse a heavenly army, or shatter the staff of the Monkey King himself. But holding it is not a privilege; it is a sentence. Every artifact it captures leaves a scar of Killing Energy inside the band, slowly turning the ring into a lead weight that drags its wielder toward madness, unless that wielder is the one being who forged it—the Supreme Elderly Lord himself.

body.body_1:
金刚琢 / Adamantine Band

后天至宝 (Postcelestial Supreme Treasure)

Artifact Tier: Tai Gu Shen Bing (Primordial Divine Armament)
Current Holder: Supreme Elderly Lord (太上老君 / Taishang Laojun)
Current Status: Returned to Laozi; presumed sealed or housed within the Tushita Palace in the Celestial Realm.
body.body_2: The Adamantine Band belongs to the class of Postcelestial Supreme Treasures, forged after the Honghuang Era yet rivaling the might of innate primordial weapons. Its core function is the capture and nullification of all weapons and treasures within the Three Realms. The band is highly adaptable, capable of changing its size and trajectory mid-flight to intercept any projectile or artifact. It is impervious to water, fire, and most forms of assault. Its most famous recorded feat was a single blow that defeated Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, and shattered his Golden-Banded Staff (金箍棒), the very staff that had once served as the Ocean-Settling Divine Needle. The external surface of the band is inscribed with one hundred and twenty thousand Seal-Collecting Talismans, which activate upon contact with a captured object. To wield the band safely, one must possess a cultivation base that can withstand the accumulated Sha Qi (Killing Energy) inside the ring. In practice, only Taishang Laojun himself has demonstrated the capacity to use it without fatal repercussions.
body.body_3: The Adamantine Band was forged using Heaven and Earth as the furnace and the energies of Creation and Transformation—Primal Yin and Primal Yang—as its foundation. The primary structural material is Jiu Zhuan Bin Tie (Nine-Cycle Refined Iron), a celestial metal that has undergone nine cycles of smelting, folding, and quenching to achieve exceptional purity. Into this iron matrix were blended Xuan Tian Iron Ore (九天玄铁) and the essence of the Five Metals (五金精华). The forging process took place within the Eight Trigram Furnace (八卦炉) of the Tushita Palace, requiring a continuous forty-nine years of refinement. During this period, Laozi expended a vast quantity of his own primordial true essence to sustain the fire and the internal formations. The most severe cost was the Blood Sacrifice (血祭): the lifeblood of one hundred species of divine beasts was injected into the molten metal, with each beast's blood added at the Zi hour (the time of the Rat, midnight) in a ritual that continued unbroken for one hundred years. The accumulated blood essence permanently altered the metal's spiritual composition, imbuing the band with an inherent hunger for other artifacts' power.
body.body_4: The Adamantine Band does not contain a sealed living soul as its Qi Ling (Artifact Spirit). Its spiritual agency is not a bound prisoner but an emergent consciousness born from the union of the Nine-Cycle Refined Iron, the combined blood essence of the hundred divine beasts, and the forging power of the Eight Trigram Furnace. This consciousness is not a personality in the human sense; it is a singular, obsessive drive to capture, hold, and absorb other artifacts. The band possesses a primitive will of its own, capable of pursuing targets independently and even choosing to ignore its wielder's commands when a more powerful artifact presents itself. This will is fueled by the residual Killing Energy (Sha Qi) that accumulates within the band each time it captures an object. Over the centuries, this accumulation has made the band heavier and more difficult to control, requiring Laozi to cleanse it every sixty years using Xian Tian Yi Qi (Primordial Breath) to prevent the accumulated Sha Qi from overwhelming the band's internal matrix.
body.body_5: The bond between the Adamantine Band and its wielder is not a master-servant relationship but a conditional symbiosis with a lethal threshold. The band does not require a formal Ren Zhu (Master Recognition) ceremony such as blood-dropping or soul-binding. Rather, it recognizes the power and authority of the one who holds it. For Taishang Laojun—the being who forged it—the band is a compliant instrument. For anyone else, the band's accumulated Sha Qi (Killing Energy) acts as an active threat. If a wielder's cultivation is insufficient, the Sha Qi will parasitically drain their life force and erode their consciousness. Historical records from the Tushita Palace describe a disciple who secretly stole the band and attempted to wield it. The Sha Qi inside the ring overwhelmed the disciple within hours, transforming them into a soulless puppet—a vacant-shell servant driven only by the band's primal directive to capture. The band does not actively seek to "devour" its master in the manner of a malevolent sentient artifact, but it will passively consume any wielder too weak to resist its accumulated malice.
body.body_6: Only one stable wielder is recorded for the Adamantine Band in established mythology: Taishang Laojun himself. The band was forged by Laozi for his own use and has remained under his possession throughout its recorded history. The single recorded instance of another being holding the band is the disciple mentioned in BODY_5, whose name has been lost to tradition. That disciple's fate—being consumed into a puppet—serves as the only known case of Master Argeting (噬主) through the band's passive Sha Qi effect. No other figures are documented as having successfully claimed or wielded the band. The tradition emphasizes that the band is, by design, an extension of Laozi's own authority and cannot be meaningfully commanded by any other being in the Three Realms.
body.body_7: The most famous recorded activation of the Adamantine Band occurred during the conflict between Sun Wukong and the Celestial Court. During a pitched battle, Laozi threw the band from the Heaven-Reaching Gate. The band flew down, struck Sun Wukong directly on the head, and in that single blow, shattered the Golden-Banded Staff (金箍棒). The band then looped around Wukong's torso and bound him, rendering the Great Sage Equal to Heaven completely immobile. This single activation demonstrated the band's capacity to neutralize the most physically powerful being in the known mythos at the time. There is no recorded instance of the band's power reaching a quantifiable "maximum" or "limit," nor any tradition of the band being used so aggressively that it damaged itself. The band's natural function—absorbing artifacts—generates a continuous buildup of Sha Qi, which Laozi periodically cleanses to prevent the band from becoming too heavy to throw accurately. The tradition implies a gradual, incremental burden rather than a sudden failure threshold.
body.body_8: The Adamantine Band has no recorded paired or complementary artifact. It is depicted as a singular creation of Taishang Laojun, not part of a set. The most significant recorded interaction is with two other artifacts: the Golden-Banded Staff (金箍棒) of Sun Wukong, which the band shattered in a single blow, and the Plantain Leaf Fan (芭蕉扇), which legend treats as another of Laozi's notable treasures, though the two artifacts' direct relationship is not established in the primary source material. There is no tradition of a dedicated counter-artifact designed to resist the Adamantine Band. Within the established mythos, the band is portrayed as effectively uncounterable by any artifact-level means, needing either the direct intervention of a being of Laozi's own stature or the withdrawal of the band by its wielder. The band is not derived from the remains of a higher-tier primordial weapon.
body.body_9: The current status of the Adamantine Band is stable. After its use against Sun Wukong, the band was returned to Taishang Laojun. Within the standard narrative tradition, the band remains in Laozi's possession, stored or sealed within the Tushita Palace in the Celestial Realm. It is not known to be awaiting a new master, as its nature makes it effectively inseparable from its creator. There is no tradition of the band having been destroyed, lost, or having its spiritual essence degraded to the point of dormancy.
body.body_10: None. No dedicated monuments, storage sites, or physical records documenting the forging process of the Adamantine Band are referenced in the canonical tradition. The primary literary source for the band is the 16th-century novel *Journey to the West* (《西游记》), particularly the chapters recounting the conflict with Sun Wukong and the intervention of the Supreme Elderly Lord.
body.body_11: The Adamantine Band's most dramatic recorded appearance involves Sun Wukong (孙悟空), the Monkey King of the Water Curtain Cave. Earlier in the narrative, Sun Wukong's own weapon, the Golden-Banded Staff (金箍棒), was extracted from the Eastern Sea and wielded with devastating effect. When the band shatters the staff, it signals the peak of Wukong's rebellion and the necessity of a direct intervention by the highest celestial authority. The band is a product of the Tushita Palace (兜率宫), the personal domain of the Supreme Elderly Lord, a realm known for the production of other legendary artifacts. The tradition also places the band in implicit comparison with the Planting Leaf Fan (芭蕉扇), another weapon of Laozi's creation, known for its mastery over fire through pure Yin Qi.

guide.guide_1: Imagine, if you will, a ring. Not a wedding band, not a class ring, and definitely not the kind of bracelet you pick up at a craft fair. Imagine a heavy, cold, thrumming circle of metal that has been designed with a single, focused purpose: to close its grip on anything that is too powerful, too chaotic, or too defiant. That is the Adamantine Band. If you are familiar with mythological weapons of the West, think of Thor's hammer Mjolnir, but built not to smash enemies—to *collect* them. The band is a jaw. When it clamps down on a god's weapon, that god is not just disarmed; they have just been shown a brutal lesson in who truly owns the power in this universe. And here is the part that never makes it into the bedtime stories: every time it catches a weapon, a little piece of that weapon's violence, its Shā Qì—a kind of concentrated lethal intent—gets stored inside the ring. Over centuries, that accumulation makes the band heavier, meaner, and far more dangerous to the person holding it than to the person it is thrown at.
guide.guide_2: If you have read *Journey to the West* or seen any of its countless adaptations, you know the Adamantine Band. You may know it as the object that, without any warning, falls from the sky and knocks Sun Wukong's head, breaking his legendary staff in one blow. It is often presented as a moment of divine trickery—a magical item used by an old god to win a fight. But the representation misses the actual weight of the moment. That ring was not just a tool. It was the creator's authority made physical. The fact that it could break the staff that had been the *Ocean-Settling Divine Needle*—a weapon that had once held back a sea—is the narrative telling you something uncomfortable: there is always a bigger power, a deeper hunger, a more ancient cost behind every flash of victory. Let us dig into what that ring actually is, and why holding it is never just an honor.
guide.guide_3: To understand the band, we have to start with the steel. It is not any steel; it is Jiu Zhuan Bin Tie—"Nine-Cycle Refined Iron." Imagine a metal that has been smelted, folded, and quenched not once or twice, but *nine times* to achieve perfect purity. Into that iron, Laozi blended Xuan Tian Iron Ore and the essence of the Five Metals. These materials are not pretty metaphors; they represent the physical skeleton of the universe. To forge such a band, you need an impossible furnace—the Eight Trigram Furnace, which can manage the heat needed to melt celestial metals. But the real horror is the blood. The forging required the lifeblood of one hundred species of divine beasts, each one injected into the molten metal at a specific, inauspicious hour—the Zi hour, midnight—for one hundred years straight. This was not a symbolic offering. This was a long-term, systematic draining of divine vitality. The band does not just work; it works because it was fed on the life force of a hundred different kinds of ancient power. That is the cost of creating a tool that can steal the power of other tools. This is not "materials cost" in any normal sense; this is a century of serial sacrifice.
guide.guide_4: Here is where things get morally tricky. The band does not have a "sealed soul" in the same way that, say, a cursed sword from a particular cycle of the Táohuā Shān myths might have. There is no captured warrior, no betrayed disciple screaming inside the ring. Instead, the band has an *emergent consciousness*—a mind born from the combination of the refined iron, the blood of the hundred beasts, and the furnace fire. It is not a person. It is an urge. It is a hunger to capture. The band can think, in a rudimentary way. It can track a target. It can *choose* not to obey its wielder if it senses a more potent artifact within reach. This is the "artifact spirit" (Qi Ling) in its most disturbing form: not a ghost with memories, but a pure, unfiltered impulse to consume power. Its conscience is a void shaped by a millennia of accumulated Killing Energy (Sha Qi) from every weapon it has ever absorbed. When you hold it, you are not holding a pet. You are holding a predator with its own internal ecology, one that is increasingly hostile to you the longer it lives.
guide.guide_5: So, how does the band let someone hold it? No blood-dropping ceremony, no soul-binding pact. The band is not a fan of bureaucracy. It simply *recognizes* authority. For Taishang Laojun, who forged it out of his own will, the band is docile. It listens. For anyone else, the problem is the Shā Qì. The accumulated lethal energy inside the band does not differentiate between "master" and "target"; it presses against *any* consciousness that tries to command it. A disciple once stole the band. Within hours, the band's internal pressure overwhelmed his mind, and he became a puppet. Not dead, but vacant—a living shell driven by the band's command to capture. If you are strong enough to withstand the pressure, the band will obey you, but it will also *use* you. It will keep demanding you use it to capture things, feeding its own hunger. Every cycle makes it heavier, harder to control. Every cycle, the pressure rises. This is not a partnership. This is a temporary ceasefire between a weak stomach and a very hungry stomach.
guide.guide_6: In all of recorded mythology, only one name is reliably attached to the Adamantine Band: Taishang Laojun. He is the creator, the sole stable wielder. The one other recorded attempt to hold it—a now-anonymous disciple of the Tushita Palace—ended in that horrific puppet-fication. The tragedy of that disciple is not recorded with sentimentality; it is recorded as a warning. The message is clear: do not pick up a weapon built by a creator god unless you *are* that creator god. There are no hero stories about the band, no epic where a mortal rose to tame it. The band does not elevate heroes; it exposes pretenders. This singularity is refreshing compared to many mythological weapons that pass through a dozen hands. The band's narrative function is to be the final authority, not a recycled trophy.
guide.guide_7: So, why is the Adamantine Band designed to be so unforgiving? Because this universe operates on a brutal but coherent principle: any power that is not *yours* must be paid for. You cannot borrow a god's authority for free. The band is the cost, the receipt, and the prison all in one. It is not that every weapon in the Eastern cosmos is a furnace of trapped souls—the band itself shows a subtler, more structural horror. The cost is not a hostage; it is an *inevitable accumulation*. The more you use something beyond your station, the heavier that something becomes. It drags you down, fills your mind with Shā Qì, and eventually empties you out. The band is a mirror for the entire logic of this mythology: if you reach for a power you did not earn, the universe will make you pay. And in the end, the only one who can hold the band without being ground to dust is the only one who built it with his own hands.

seo.meta_description: The Adamantine Band is a Postcelestial Supreme Treasure of the Supreme Elderly Lord. A ring forged to capture any divine weapon, it shattered Sun Wukong's staff and bound the Monkey King. But every capture leaves a scar of Killing Energy inside the band, making it a tool that consumes weak wielders and grants ultimate power only to its creator.
seo.og_title: 金刚琢 / Adamantine Band – A Ring That Steals the Power of Gods
seo.og_description: A Postcelestial Supreme Treasure forged by the Supreme Elderly Lord. The Adamantine Band can disarm any god and break any weapon, but its accumulated Killing Energy turns it into a death sentence for any wielder but its creator. Explore its materials, its blood-soaked forging, and the fate of the disciple who tried to steal it.
seo.twitter_title: 金刚琢 / Adamantine Band – The Ring That Broke Sun Wukong’s Staff
seo.twitter_description: A Postcelestial Supreme Treasure that can capture any artifact. Forged with blood from a hundred divine beasts, it shattered the Golden-Banded Staff and bound the Monkey King. The only safe wielder is its creator, the Supreme Elderly Lord.

lore_entries.description: Nine-Cycle Refined Iron; a celestial metal that has undergone nine rounds of smelting, folding, and quenching to achieve extreme purity and strength.
A rare celestial iron from the ninth heaven, used as a primary material in the band's forging.
The refined essence of the five sacred metals—gold, silver, copper, iron, and tin—added to the band's alloy.
The alchemical furnace of the Tushita Palace used by the Supreme Elderly Lord to forge divine artifacts and elixirs.
The 120,000 talismans inscribed on the band's surface that activate upon contact with a captured object.
The hour of the Rat (midnight), the sacred time at which each of the hundred divine beasts' blood was added to the forge.
The personal realm of the Supreme Elderly Lord in the Celestial Realm, the forge and home of the Adamantine Band.
The buildup of Killing Energy inside the band over time, which makes the ring heavier and more dangerous.

faq_entries.question: How did the Adamantine Band defeat Sun Wukong?
faq_entries.answer: Laozi threw the band from the Heaven-Reaching Gate. It struck Sun Wukong on the head, shattered his Golden-Banded Staff in a single blow, then looped around his torso and bound the Great Sage Equal to Heaven completely.

faq_entries.question: Can anyone use the Adamantine Band besides Laozi?
faq_entries.answer: In theory, yes, but the accumulated Killing Energy inside the band will overwhelm any wielder whose cultivation is insufficient. A documented case exists of a disciple who tried to use it and was transformed into a soulless puppet within hours.

faq_entries.question: Does the Adamantine Band have a sealed soul inside it?
faq_entries.answer: No. It does not contain a trapped human or beast soul. Instead, it has an emergent consciousness born from the fusion of refined iron, the blood of a hundred divine beasts, and the forging process. This consciousness is a pure drive to capture artifacts, not a personality.

faq_entries.question: What happened to the band after it was used?
faq_entries.answer: It was returned to Taishang Laojun and is presumed to be stored or sealed within the Tushita Palace in the Celestial Realm.
